title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and EM
text: Many data health research counts: number hospital visits month, number research papers published. Poisson regression useful case, strong assumption: mean variance must equal. rarely true real data set. count data overdispersed, variance greater mean, many data sets also contain zeros Poisson distribution allows. negative binomial (NB2) model handles overdispersion dispersion parameter θ\theta, Var(Y)=μ+μ2/θ\mathrm{Var}(Y) = \mu + \mu^2/\theta. extra zeros come different process, example person never sees doctor, zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model fits naturally. treats observation either structural zero draw NB distribution, can zero. project, built R package nbzinbHossen, fits models: NB regression iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS), alternated Newton–Raphson updates log⁡θ\log\theta; ZINB regression EM algorithm whose M-steps IRLS fits. use general-purpose optimizer optim(), glm() fitting code. check package MASS::glm.nb() pscl::zeroinfl() two data sets, test simulation whether zinbreg() recovers known parameters, use analyse NMES1988 data.

title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and EM
text: package reproduces glm.nb() zeroinfl() closely without general-purpose optimizer, approach limits. Speed. EM converges linearly (Figure 1): zinbreg() needed 66 iterations NMES1988 135 bioChemists, ran 5 9 times slower zeroinfl(). SQUAREM acceleration, switching Newton’s method observed-data likelihood EM near optimum, cut . NB standard errors. Like glm.nb(), nbreg() treats θ\theta known computing SE(β̂)\mathrm{SE}(\hat\beta), SEs ignore uncertainty θ̂\hat\theta. Interval coverage. simulation showed Wald intervals -covering slightly n=500n = 500 (0.905 binary covariate). Profile-likelihood bootstrap intervals reliable. Local maxima. EM can principle stop local maximum, results depend starting values. (NB fit plus logistic regression zero indicator) reached optimum zeroinfl() every case tried, guaranteed. Offsets. Offsets supported count part. Natural extensions zero-inflated Poisson option, hurdle models, robust (sandwich) standard errors, probit complementary log-log link zero part, Vuong test comparing NB ZINB.

text: nbzinbHossen fits negative binomial (NB2) regression nbreg() (alternative MASS::glm.nb()), using iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) coefficients alternated Newton–Raphson log(θ); zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression zinbreg() (alternative pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin")), using EM algorithm whose M-steps IRLS fits (fractional-response logistic regression zero part weighted NB regression count part). general-purpose optimizer (optim(), nlm(), …) glm()/lm() fitting code used. ZINB standard errors come analytic Hessian observed-data log-likelihood. Website (function reference + project report): https://armanhossen-.github.io/nbzinbHossen/

Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression via IRLS
text: fitting functions return S3 objects print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik (AIC()/BIC() work), fitted, residuals, nobs predict methods. Use nbreg_control() / zinbreg_control() change tolerances, iteration limits, print iteration history (trace = TRUE).
code: library(nbzinbHossen) data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")  # Negative binomial regression nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists) summary(nb) nb$theta                     # 2.264, same as MASS::glm.nb()  # Zero-inflated NB: count covariates | zero-inflation covariates zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,                 data = bioChemists) summary(zinb) AIC(nb, zinb)  # Predictions: marginal mean, NB mean, and structural-zero probability nd <- data.frame(fem = "Women", mar = "Married", kid5 = 1, phd = 3, ment = 10) predict(zinb, newdata = nd, type = "response") predict(zinb, newdata = nd, type = "count") predict(zinb, newdata = nd, type = "zero")

what: Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM — zinbreg
title: Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM — zinbreg
text: Fits ZINB model $$P(Y_i = 0) = \pi_i + (1 - \pi_i) f_{NB}(0; \mu_i, \theta), \quad       P(Y_i = y) = (1 - \pi_i) f_{NB}(y; \mu_i, \theta),\ y \ge 1,$$ \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\), EM algorithm. E-step computes posterior probability \(\tau_i\) observation \(\) structural zero; M-step fits logistic regression fractional response \(\tau_i\) IRLS (zero part) weighted NB regression prior weights \(1 - \tau_i\) nbreg()'s IRLS / Newton-Raphson algorithm (count part). Standard errors come observed information observed-data log-likelihood \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\). results agree pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin").
